legend: Consider all divisors of some integer n$$$n$$$. Choose some of these divisors, then arrange them in a circle so that the ratio of any two adjacent numbers is a prime number.
Find the maximum number of divisors of n$$$n$$$ you can choose, and find the appropriate arrangement.
input: The first line of input contains the integer n$$$n$$$ (2≤n≤109$$$2 \le n \le 10^9$$$).
output: In the first line, print a single integer k$$$k$$$ — the maximum number of divisors of n$$$n$$$ you can choose.

In the second line, print k$$$k$$$ integers — different divisors of n$$$n$$$ in the order they appear on the circle. Any two adjacent and the first and last numbers in this list must differ by multiplication by some prime number.
